This is my participation A post. I have an executive summary and then the full logs attached. Please let me know if there is anything wrong with my format and I will repost. 

Joseph Berry
 CS182 HW 1 
 Claude Answer Analysis

I used Claude Model Opus 4.1, with the Research button activated allowing for “Agentic mode” or web searches while answering a question. 

This model was able to one shot most of the questions. It failed on questions 2 and 3 and was unable to compute the eigenvalues or discriminant of part 3 without help. Even when presented with the correct answer. 

Problem 1. Why Learning Rates Cannot be Too Big
 Part a.

 Answered the question completely.
Part b. 
 Solved the question, then proceeded to give me a second answer it thought was equivalent and an example with numerical value. 

Part c.

 Solved the question but arrived at a different solution of 2/σ^2 instead of 1/σ^2. Also defined loss L(W) as 1/2|| y – Σw ||^2 instead of || y – Σw ||^2. It claimed the ½ was a “convenience factor” making the gradient slightly easier to compute, and that it would lead to a different effective learning rate, which it didn’t believe was an issue. 

Part d.

 Solved the question and then continued explaining which σ value, large or small, would converge faster.

Part e.

Gave a slightly incorrect answer:
 η= 1/(σℓ 2 + σs 2 ) = 1/(σℓ 2) instead of the course solution 1/(σℓ 2 + σs 2 )

Part f.

 Answered the question mathematically instead of using definitions. 

Problem 2. Stochastic Gradient Descent (when it is possible to interpolate)

Part a.

 Full Solution.

Part b.

 Full Solution.

Part c.

 Found the correct answer then continued creating coordinate changes, and tried to create a formula for the coordinate changes. 

Part d.

 Full Solution. 

Part e.

 Claude wasn’t able to produce the correct solution, but provided a similar solution (missing expectation of loss, just had loss) and then proceeded to try and show how the problem scaled with just σ and ε. It was able to produce an answer that loss goes to 0 as t goes to infinity. 

Part f.

 Full Solution. 

Part g.

 Full Solution. 

Part h.

 Gave the correct answer but left out the learning rate term from c1. When asked why c1 did not include the learning rate it stated that the learning rate “By keeping η\eta η separate, we can later analyze how to choose η\eta η optimally”

Part i.

 Gave a solution without including the learning rate like in Part h. But also left out the Rho value, or any equivalent value, for the largest norm of the rows of coordinate shifted X. Then when asked if it could include a value representing this, it gave out the answer without including sigma max but now including Rho. 
 When asked again it stated that sigma max and rho would be the same value. Stating that both solutions, including rho and excluding rho were correct. 

Part j.

 Full Solution. 

Part k. 

 This question required reading a jupyter notebook. After inputting Claude explained a small amount about standard ridge regression and feature augmentation. 

 Problem 3. Accelerating Gradient Descent with Momentum

Part a. 

 Full Solution.

Part b. 

 Full Solution.

Part c. 

 At this problem Claude took over 3 minutes “compiling source” from the internet to provide a solution. I interrupted this and then repeated the question. Claude then gave me an incorrect answer for the discriminant and answers for eigenvalues that didn’t include the square root term. 

Part d. 

 Incorrect answer, due to an incorrect solution for part a. I then supplied it with the correct solution for part a. After giving it the correct discriminant and eigenvalues it still produced an incorrect answer. 

Part e. 

 Incorrect solution.

Part f. 

 Full Solution

Part g. 

 Gave a close answer for Ordinary Gradient Descent (342 where true answer was 346) And a wildly incorrect answer for the momentum version (919 where true answer was 132)

Part h.

 I skipped this question, it required a jupyter notebook

Part i. 

  I skipped this question, it required a jupyter notebook

Part b.

5. Regularization and Instance Noise

Part a. 

 Full Solution. 

Part b. 

 Failed to produce the correct answer, was given hints on how to find the correct answer answer. On third prompt I gave it the correct answer and asked it to work backwards. It claimed that it needed to know that this was for the scalar case in order to give a correct answer. 

Part c. 

 Full Solution
